# Variety generated by an algebra

The variety generated by an algebra is the class of all algebras of its type that satisfy every identity true in it; it is the least variety containing the algebra.

Let $A$ be an [algebra](algebras-of-a-finite-type.md) of a finite type $\tau$. The *variety generated* by $A$, written $\mathcal{V}(A)$, is the class of all algebras of type $\tau$ that [satisfy](identities-satisfied-by-an-algebra.md) every identity satisfied by $A$. It is a [variety](varieties-of-algebras-and-finitely-generated-varieties.md), and it is contained in every variety that contains $A$.
